column1: # Engine perf suite rows, the lowest median of each in microseconds, checked
# by scripts/regress/perf-ratchet.sh (the perf-suite leg, scripts/regress.sh
# linux --perf). One row<TAB>microseconds record per line; a row is named
# <section> | <label> as the suite prints them, whitespace collapsed. A row
# fails when it is more than 10% and more than 5 us over its value here, and an
# unlisted row fails. Wall times only compare on the machine named by #host;
# anywhere else the leg is a SKIP, and CI never runs it.
# Lower values after a fix with: bash scripts/regress/perf-ratchet.sh --update
# It only lowers values and drops rows the suite no longer runs. Raising a
# value or adding a row is a hand edit, and the change has to say why.
# Recorded with the 0.17 candidate (5fa8c095), the lowest of eight runs. Every
# row was re-recorded there, 35 up and 21 down from the values before it,
# because every mixer compressor became Multi-Comp 2, which runs at its own 2x
# whatever Effect Oversampling says. At Effect Oversampling 1x a row with the
# compressors in costs up to 3.1 times what it did at 48 kHz and up to 1.6
# times at 96 kHz. At 2x it costs 1.4 times as much at 48 kHz. At 4x, and at
# 96 kHz from 2x, it costs less than before: the compressor left the strip's
# oversampler. With the compressors out a row costs less, since a compressor
# that is out is not run.
#host;
